Apple's chip manufacturing partner TSMC had previously stated plans to build a total of eight fabrication plants in Arizona, and has now announced an expanded investment that could increase the number to as many as twelve.

This move may result in more chips used in Apple devices being produced in the United States, but there are reasons to remain skeptical about this possibility…

A TSMC chip fabrication plant in Arizona

Almost exactly one year ago today, TSMC announced it would accelerate construction of its second and third fabrication plants in Arizona. Apple was designated as the first customer for the third plant.

Some observers have questioned how much practical significance American chip production holds for Apple devices. One reason is that TSMC deliberately restricts its most advanced manufacturing processes to its fabs in its home country of Taiwan. The planned American plants are simply incapable of producing the chips needed for the latest Apple devices.

This means that only chips for older-model Apple devices—generally around three generations behind—can be produced in the United States. Even so, skepticism remains, because bare chips are only one step in the entire process. Apple's chips are actually composed of multiple different chips integrated through a procedure known as 'packaging,' and the original plan was to send the American-manufactured chips back to Taiwan for packaging.

One analyst therefore described the Arizona plant as nothing more than a 'paperweight.' There was briefly some discussion about entrusting packaging to a third-party American company, after which TSMC stated it would establish its own chip packaging facility in the United States.

Since then, the total number of planned American plants has increased to eight.

New investment may bring the number of American plants to twelve

The Trump administration has now announced that TSMC has agreed to an additional one hundred billion US dollars in investment in American facilities, claiming this will bring the total number of Arizona plants to twelve—though this figure includes both packaging and chip manufacturing facilities.

However, the picture TSMC itself paints is somewhat different. According to BBC News, TSMC has only stated that its expanded investment 'may' result in the construction of four new plants, and has not provided any timeline whatsoever.

Apple is also seeking partnerships with other chip manufacturers such as Intel and Samsung, which may further affect the 'market conditions' cited by TSMC when making this announcement.

In other words, this has all the hallmarks of a political announcement: promoting an eye-catching number for something that may or may not happen, without any timeline having been released.
